classification.difficultyReason: Link simultaneous intersection and axis intercepts with triangle area, choosing the coordinate distance perpendicular to each axis base without a supplied sketch. The named axes and prior taught area method guide the linked procedures.

content.prompt: Find the area of the triangle formed by the lines $x+3y=6$, $y=5-x$ and:

answer.worked:
The $x$-intercepts are $(6,0)$ and $(5,0)$, so the base has length $1$.
At the intersection:
$$\begin{align*}x+3(5-x)&=6\\15-2x&=6\\x&=\frac92\\y&=5-\frac92\\y&=\frac12\end{align*}$$
Check: $\frac92+3(\frac12)=6$.
The perpendicular height is $\frac12$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12\times1\times\frac12\\A&=\frac14\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored solution sketch showing the triangle, its horizontal base and perpendicular height; the y-axis lies outside this local view.

answer.worked:
The $y$-intercepts are $(0,2)$ and $(0,5)$, so the base has length $3$.
At the intersection:
$$\begin{align*}x+3(5-x)&=6\\15-2x&=6\\x&=\frac92\\y&=5-\frac92\\y&=\frac12\end{align*}$$
Check: $\frac92+3(\frac12)=6$.
The perpendicular height is the horizontal distance $\frac92$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12\times3\times\frac92\\A&=\frac{27}{4}\text{ square units}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored solution sketch showing the vertical base on the y-axis and the horizontal perpendicular height.
